feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid public-sector experience. It shows breadth and progression well, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo and a well-defined niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility signals: scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) and concrete platforms/tools strengthen impact.  
- Broad but relevant skill mix: combines strategy, technical execution, analytics, and multimedia in a way that fits senior digital roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears across multiple sections; consolidate Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT to avoid overlap.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or cost savings where possible.  
- Fix writing/style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler; capitalization is inconsistent (“Coleman DAVIS” vs normal title case); punctuation style varies across bullets and sections.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience; adding one concrete scale marker would sharpen impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce the long list of functions; group related capabilities.
- Add 1–2 concrete scale signals already evidenced in the CV (e.g., 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).
- Use parallel wording and hyphenation consistently: “AI-enabled,” “public sector” or “public-sector” (pick one style and keep it consistent).
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, and multimedia programs—most notably a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers—while advancing AI-enabled search and user experience for mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list repeats core competencies almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less sentence-like capability areas and aligned more clearly with senior leadership positioning.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and shorten phrasing for faster scanning.
- Use parallel noun-based terms; avoid mixing systems, operations, and outcomes in one list.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space is tight, reduce to 6 items by merging multimedia with multi-channel communications and folding advocacy into public-sector communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” duplicate the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also repeated in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads more like dense prose than a quick “selected projects” snapshot. Tightening the wording and emphasizing outcomes or scope will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Rename to “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as a concise one-line project summary with parallel structure.
- Add specificity where possible: audience, platform, scale, or outcome (for example, “Drupal 10 microsite,” “legislative search,” “conference display”).
- Tighten phrasing: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future campaign expansion”; use “10 x 20-foot” for style consistency.
- Consider this rewrite: AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and reusable modules for expansion.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series substantially overlap with current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most distinct value because it introduces experiential/display work not highlighted elsewhere.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + hands-on scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the projects section and prior NACo work. Tighten around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this consulting level.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client scope: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations modernization.”
- Consolidate bullets into 4–5 sharper points; combine “digital systems/workflows/analytics” with governance/operations to reduce repetition.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, time saved, stakeholder teams served, or engagement/performance improvements.
- Emphasize distinctive recent work: AI-enabled search, Drupal campaign architecture, enterprise workflow design, and cross-channel governance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level and save technical specifics for Projects.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement echo the NACo Director role; stress consulting/embedded leadership and current delivery.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Combine and streamline the website bullet: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused: add email/social growth, engagement, CTR, list size, or campaign performance if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten operations bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve decision-making” plus one governance bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo roles; emphasize building the studio, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Make it sharper by emphasizing scope, ownership, and outcomes distinct from the later director role and earlier producer role.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for county officials nationwide.”
- Replace “helping” language with ownership verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters… Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update… Built/standardized editorial planning… Improved publishing workflows…”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter audience size, open/click rates, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, publishing volume, or workflow time saved.
- Consider this rewrite: “Managed NACo’s daily digital communications operations across web, email, social and video. Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders; produced a recurring advocacy video update; and strengthened cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this role as scaling/operationalizing the series.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this entry focused on execution-level ownership rather than governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- SharePoint

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal basics like “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” here; keep those in Technical + IT unless they are central to target roles.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation.
- If space allows, make one phrase outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the exact phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure & performance optimization” instead of “Analytics, Insights & Optimization.”
- Tighten to 5–7 items that show seniority: “Analytics strategy (GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio) • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity) • SEO and content performance optimization”
- Group tools in parentheses rather than listing each separately; this saves space and feels more strategic.
- If accurate, strengthen with scope language: “enterprise reporting,” “cross-channel performance analysis,” or “decision-ready dashboards.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current tool list duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies unless phrased more distinctly.

  “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • In-house studio operations • Virtual event production”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light proficiency framing if space allows: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If you want stronger impact, rename the heading to **CMS Platforms** or **Web Platforms (CMS)** for concision.
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful recent use; it reads lighter than the enterprise/public-sector platforms above.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely repeats the **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution** entry; keep one more strategic and this one purely tool-based.
- Avoid adding “CMS modernization” here—that concept is already covered in Topline Skills and work experience.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should emphasize implementation depth and modern, relevant tools tied to current work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a tighter, more current list: **Front-end & Technical Implementation:** HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (**HTML5, CSS3**) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value.
- Consider removing **jQuery** or placing it last as “legacy support” if still relevant; it can date the profile versus the stronger recent tools.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in parentheses, e.g. **API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)** or **GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: **“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations • Workflow automation.”**
- **Google Tag Manager** may fit better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** if you want cleaner categorization.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this section should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first: keep Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Teams; consider dropping weaker/older items if space is tight.
- If possible, add light context in another section rather than here, e.g., “built cross-team publishing and reporting workflows” to show impact.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clarity and specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools and may add little value unless central to your systems work.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this reads as a bare software list with no signal on depth or scale. Since email operations already appear in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused rather than restating newsletter work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level of use without repeating experience bullets, e.g. **campaign setup, segmentation, automation, newsletter operations**
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform first; if Higher Logic or Dynamics was central in 2022–2024, place that tool first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or audience reach here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item tool-specific

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization capabilities, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation**
- Swap “A/B testing” for **Experimentation** unless you’ve run formal tests; it sounds more credible and broader.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with **KPI reporting** or **Executive reporting** to show business use, not just output format.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider removing one or making this section tools-only and the topline section outcomes/capabilities-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” and team-building contributions without repeating later leadership claims.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and sharpen impact: “Improved workflows across web, email, social and multimedia; supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video content.”
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” and “day-to-day guidance” with specifics or outcomes if available: audience size, production cadence, event count, traffic/email gains, or team size.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Improved workflows across web, email, social and multimedia; supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and supervised a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate by framing this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Keep it brief, emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator, and add any scale or outputs if available.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; also supported digital storytelling and multimedia production.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- If possible, add measurable detail: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or number/type of research projects delivered.
- Remove filler like “contributed to” and “materials”; use stronger verbs such as coordinated, produced, launched, or delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Multimedia production appears repeatedly in later NACo roles; avoid overexplaining video/content work here.
- Don’t frame this as broad digital leadership—that is already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with current/relevant production strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
